item.title: J. Cole Shares Birmingham Spotlight With Fans & Finds Fayetteville Native In The Crowd
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: J. Cole shared the spotlight with four Birmingham fans and sang "Nobody's Perfect" with the crowd during his arena show.
item.content:encoded:
J. Cole chose four fans to rap “Johnny P’s Caddy” on camera at his October 25 Birmingham show in the United Kingdom.

Footage showed fans had held up signs asking to trade bars with him. The crowd also backed him on an almost a cappella “Nobody’s Perfect.”

Cole praised Birmingham and hometown heroes Black Sabbath, while fans waved white towels during “Old Dog,” according to local reports. Incredibly, he also spotted a fan from his hometown of Fayetteville.

The two-hour set began with Cole singing “39 Intro” under a spotlight among the audience. He walked through standing fans, clasping hands, before a car and house appeared onstage. He later sang “Poor Thang” from the roof. “Quik Stop” closed the show.

The stop took place at Utilita Arena Birmingham as part of “The Fall-Off Tour.” The venue billed the run as his first UK headline shows since 2017, a nine-year gap between his UK headline runs.

That return followed the February 6 release of The Fall-Off, his seventh studio album. As AllHipHop previously reported, Cole announced a tour of more than 50 dates across North America, Europe, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa. The original plan covered more than 15 countries, with an opening night in Charlotte and a December 12 finale in Johannesburg.

The run was his first solo headline tour since “The Off-Season Tour” in 2021. It also marked his first full world tour since 2017’s “4 Your Eyez Only World Tour.”

The announced itinerary linked the UK shows to dates in Paris, Hamburg, Copenhagen, Stockholm and Oslo before a late-November trip to Australia, then New Zealand and South Africa.

Home was a theme of the new album well before the stage took shape. The Fall-Off split its story across two discs, each built around a return home at a different age: 29 and 39. The idea traced two points in Cole’s pursuit of rap greatness. He had pointed toward the project on KOD in 2018 with “1985 (Intro to the ‘The Fall Off’).”

Next on his calendar was Glasgow. OVO Hydro listed Cole’s “The Fall-Off Tour” for October 26, the night after Birmingham, with tickets still on sale as of Monday morning.

item.title: Prosecutors Deny Pooh Shiesty Being Treated Inhumanely In Jail, Point to 12,000 Emails & Netflix Access
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Pooh Shiesty's prosecutors cited Netflix and thousands of emails as they opposed his complaint about isolation in jail.
item.content:encoded:
Pooh Shiesty‘s request for better jail treatment met pushback from federal lawyers who cited his Netflix access.

The Memphis rapper, born Lontrell Williams Jr., sought changes through an emergency motion filed on October 15.

His lawyers said he spent 23 hours alone each day, with only two hours a month for family visits. They said the long hours apart from others had left him anxious and unable to sleep well.

“Mr. Williams reports that the isolation is adversely affecting his mental health,” his attorneys wrote in the motion.

However, the government said he sent and received more than 12,000 emails and made about 230 video calls, FOX 4 reported. His unlimited tablet access included Netflix, NFL games, email and games, while calls totaled about 45 hours.

“It can hardly be said that these conditions of confinement are inhumane, and therefore this emergency motion should be denied outright,” U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould wrote in the response.

The government said keeping him apart protected him after he admitted taking fentanyl while in jail. Its lawyers said three inmates tried to reach him for an autograph, disrupting jail operations.

The government said his visiting hours matched those of other federal detainees, and he has had no personal visitor since August 27.

The rapper pleaded not guilty to kidnapping and conspiracy charges tied to an alleged January 10 recording studio encounter.

Prosecutors charged Pooh Shiesty alongside eight other men, including his father and fellow Memphis rapper Big30.

Federal lawyers said the men met in Dallas to discuss Pooh Shiesty’s deal with Gucci Mane’s label. They accused him of using an AK-style pistol to make a victim sign papers ending his deal.

Other men took watches, jewelry and cash while keeping the victims from leaving, the Justice Department alleged. The department said each man could spend the rest of his life in prison if found guilty.

Judge David Godbey had denied release with private guards, saying that plan would not keep others safe.

Pooh Shiesty’s trial was set for February 22, 2027, after the defense made an unopposed request, and his final pretrial conference was scheduled for February 17.

item.title: Cardi B’s Grow-Good Takes Over NYC Salon For Custom Curl Treatments
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B's Grow-Good took over a New York salon for custom hair treatments as the brand expanded into local beauty supply shops.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B‘s Grow-Good brought its haircare line into a New York salon for a day, offering treatments tailored to guests’ hair needs. The brand took over JENNA’s on 9th.

Guests received appointments tailored to their hair texture and concerns.

Cardi had spent years showing fans her natural hair routines and homemade treatments before she had products on store shelves. Her own hair masks helped spark the brand idea.

Revolve, the fashion retailer, partnered with Cardi on Grow-Good through a joint venture. Revolve told investors that Grow-Good held a presale in March before its formal April launch.

The company said every product sold out in less than an hour at both launches. Its promotion included Cardi’s North American tour, social media and Revolve Festival. Revolve also said it was increasing its investment in the joint venture.

The salon event came during a week when Grow-Good also moved into local beauty supply stores.

Its first New York shops were Beautify Beauty Supply in Harlem and Solea in the Bronx. The brand had also announced four more stores in Atlanta, Chicago, Houston and Los Angeles for October 23.

The current collection has six products, with shampoos and conditioners offered in two versions each. On the Grow-Good site, Wash Cycle Repair Shampoo and Soft Serve Repair Conditioner cost $14.99 each.

The brand sells their added “+” versions at the same price and markets them for hair that needs more moisture. Everything Serum costs $17.99, while the Get Rich Hydrating Mask is $19.99.

item.title: Conway The Machine Says Griselda Is Not Family, But Is The Group Really Finished?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Conway The Machine's startling social media comment has the internet in shambles over Griselda's brotherhood.
item.content:encoded:
Conway The Machine may have just delivered the most devastating Griselda update imaginable, and he did it with five words in a social media comment section.

“Nah we not family.”

Whew! That is a mighty peculiar statement from somebody who shares actual blood with the people he is seemingly addressing.

The Buffalo lyricist seemingly dropped that comment in response to a social media discussion about his relationship with Westside Gunn and Benny The Butcher. The internet says one hopeful thing and here comes Conway to destroy it. The remark has everybody that cares wondering if Griselda has finally reached the point of no return. Feels so…

Let’s not plan the funeral for Griselda Records yet.

First of all, Conway and Westside Gunn are half-brothers. Benny is their cousin. So, when Conway seemingly dismisses the family connection, that is much deeper than music.

READ ALSO: Westside Gunn Makes His Mass Appeal Move With HEELMATIC

And there has been plenty of disagreement.

Earlier this year, Conway sparked controversy when he removed a photograph featuring the Griselda trio from a stage during a performance. Fans immediately suspected trouble. Conway criticized people for sensationalizing the moment…saying the drama was made up.

Then podcaster Mal said Jay-Z had suggested Westside Gunn give Conway and Benny ownership stakes in Griselda. Makes sense. Some skin in the game helps everybody rise. According to Mal, Gunn declined. Gunn has since pushed back against the account and at the same time, did not clarify in any meaningful way.

Conway was singing a different tune just months ago. In May, he discussed another Griselda project and insisted there was no serious hostility between the three artists. And now we’re hearing they’re not family? Something doesn’t add up. And this is frustrating.

Griselda helped restore the brand of rugged, uncompromising lyricism we love. Their success was built on chemistry, authenticity and even that shared history way up in Buffalo.

What is the reason?

Money? Old drama coming back? Or something else?

We simply don’t know. I don’t like this soap opera.

The comment alone does not establish that Griselda has officially disbanded. And yet here we are, hoping they work it out. Hip-Hop needs more examples of brothers building together! Strength in numbers.

At the same time, I get it. I get it.

item.title: Loe Shimmy Gifts Drake A 1986 Ferrari For His 40th Birthday
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Drake received a red 1986 Ferrari Testarossa for his 40th birthday, with Loe Shimmy reportedly behind the vintage gift.
item.content:encoded:
Drake marked his 40th birthday with a gift from his own birth year: a red 1986 Ferrari Testarossa Monospecchio.

The car reportedly came from rapper Loe Shimmy. Classic car dealer Pole Position Classics found the vehicle and delivered it outside Casa Cipriani in New York, where Drake posed beside it.

The single outside mirror was a hallmark of the early Testarossa design. Ferrari mounted it high on the pillar beside the driver. Some owners added a matching mirror on the other side. In 1987, Ferrari changed the layout to two mirrors, putting one near the bottom of each side window instead of high on the pillar.

The wheels also helped place the car in its era. Early Testarossas used one central nut to secure each wheel. Ferrari changed to a five-bolt setup during 1988.

The Testarossa debuted at the Paris Motor Show in October 1984, two years before the model Drake received. Pininfarina designed the body, including the long side slats. Those openings fed air to two radiators mounted beside the engine, helping explain the wide rear end.

Under that body, the Testarossa used a flat-12 engine mounted behind the cabin. Leather trim, air conditioning and electrically adjustable seats added comfort inside. Drivers could also tilt the steering wheel to find a better position in the low car.

The celebration took place on October 23, the day before his October 24 birthday. AllHipHop previously reported on the party, which drew more than 400 friends and family members and included a surprise Backstreet Boys performance.

Inside the birthday party, guests had their own gifts to chase. Chanel and Hermès handbags were among the giveaways. A game show offered cash prizes starting in the five figures and reaching $1 million.

item.title: 50 Cent Confused After Donald Trump Calls Nicki Minaj’s Ass “Beautiful”
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: 50 Cent reacted after Donald Trump praised Nicki Minaj's backside during a Michigan rally, admitting he didn't know what was going on.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent questioned Donald Trump’s comments about Nicki Minaj’s backside after sharing footage of the president praising her during a Michigan campaign speech.

His post showed the president at a podium in C-SPAN footage, with an image of Minaj beside him.

“👀man I got feeling we fvcked, you know what’s going on because I don’t know what’s going on ! 😆.” 50 Cent wrote.

The rapper followed that thought with another line urging people to laugh, adding his Branson Cognac and Le Chemin du Roi account tags.

“LOL go ahead laugh so you don’t cry. @bransoncognac @lecheminduroi”

Minaj spent part of Sunday, October 25, traveling aboard Air Force One with Trump before his campaign appearance in Port Huron. She praised the president during an interview with White House communications director Steven Cheung.

They discussed negotiations and business, and she explained why she trusted him with the economy.

“He outworks people who are half his age,” Minaj said.

The president’s comment about Minaj came while he discussed Ohio Senator Jon Husted, whose college football background had caught his attention.

“By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before…Nicki Minaj,” Trump said. “That’s hard to miss.”

Future NFL coach Jon Gruden was Husted’s teammate at the University of Dayton, where the senator played defensive back. Trump said Gruden had described the senator’s hard tackles while recalling Husted’s years on the college team.

“I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true.”

He distinguished looking at Husted from looking at women, presenting the senator’s physique as an unusual source of interest for him.

“Off the record, women yes, men no. Okay.”

Trump discussed Husted’s physique in Youngstown on October 12 and again explained his interest in Greenville on October 20. In Michigan, his account of those earlier remarks took another turn when he brought Minaj into the story.

“Okay, I’m going to get back to my story. I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’s been with us for a long time. But anyway, so wait. So this is to show you how fake the news is. So I reveal the story.”

item.title: Victoria Monét Cancels Raleigh & New Orleans As Charlotte Show Moves
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Victoria Monét canceled Raleigh and New Orleans tour stops, moved Charlotte to November 5 and left Houston next on the schedule.
item.content:encoded:
Victoria Monét canceled two early stops on her “Frequency Of Love Tour,” leaving Raleigh and New Orleans without shows while Charlotte fans got a new date and venue.

The Raleigh concert had been set for October 27 at Red Hat Amphitheater, followed by October 30 at The Fillmore New Orleans. Ticketmaster now marks both events as canceled.

Charlotte moved from October 28 at Skyla Credit Union Amphitheater to November 5 at Ovens Auditorium. CLTure reported that Monét cited production challenges for the changes.

Fans who bought tickets for Skyla can use them at Ovens, according to the original event listing. The new show starts at 8 p.m. Ovens Auditorium is at 2900 E Independence Boulevard, Charlotte, North Carolina 28205. Doors open at 7 p.m., an hour before the show.

For Raleigh buyers, Ticketmaster says refunds will be automatic. The money goes back to the payment method used for the purchase once the organizer sends the funds, and it can take 14 to 21 days to appear. For transferred tickets, Ticketmaster sends the money to the original buyer rather than the person holding the ticket.

The Raleigh cancellation also changed which artist closed out the current Red Hat site. Monét had been booked for its last concert before the venue moves, WRAL reported. Instead, Steve Lacy played the final show there on October 23.

The sold-out concert marked the old location’s end ahead of a new amphitheater next door. June 2027 remained the target for the new venue’s opening, according to Kerry Painter of the Raleigh Convention and Performing Arts Complex. Red Hat Amphitheater opened in 2010. Plans include more than 6,000 sloped seats and permanent bathrooms.

The revised dates come after the October 2 release of Frequency of Love, her 22-song album through Lovett Music/RCA Records.

As AllHipHop previously reported, the record features SZA, Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas, with Monét’s daughter Hazel also appearing. That earlier tour plan put opening night in Raleigh.

The run marks her first tour since 2023, according to CLTure.

The next active concert on Ticketmaster’s schedule is October 31 at Houston’s 713 Music Hall.

item.title: Jakarta Makes It Rain – Literally – With Cloud Seeding Before Kanye West Show
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kanye West's Jakarta debut followed a cloud-seeding order aimed at cooling the city for his concert and a running festival.
item.content:encoded:
Kanye West‘s first concert in Indonesia came with preparations that reached beyond the stadium: Jakarta’s governor ordered cloud seeding ahead of the rapper’s show and a major running festival.

The city wanted rain before a packed weekend to bring down the heat for concertgoers, runners and residents. Ye performed Saturday, October 24, at Gelora B### Karno Main Stadium in Jakarta.

Governor Pramono Anung directed the city’s Disaster Mitigation Agency to carry out the weather operation on October 22 and 23, in coordination with Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency.

“I’ve ordered them (BPBD) to carry out cloud seeding on October 22 and 23,” Pramono said, according to Jakarta’s official news service.

That was a city order, not a special effect for a concert. The plan covered the Jakarta Running Festival and Ye’s appearance, and Pramono said rainmaking would depend on sufficient cloud cover. He also called for efforts to trigger rain through October 25, where conditions allowed.

Inside GBK, the production had a world of its own. A giant globe-shaped stage sat at the center of Ye’s performance, with a 360-degree setup that Indonesia’s Ministry of Creative Economy had highlighted in its official event listing. The listing named Raw Vision Collective and PT Global Loket Sejahtera as organizers.

The show brought to life a date announced in July. Jakarta had been billed as the only Southeast Asian stop on Ye’s 2026 tour, making the stadium appearance his first concert in Indonesia.

Medcom reporter Basuki Rachmat, who watched from the festival area, reported that Ye appeared at 9 P.M. and performed 32 tracks over nearly two hours. Fireworks, lasers and screens above the stands added to the globe-stage production.

The set included “Bound 2,” “Heartless,” “Jesus Walks” and “Ghost Town.” Rachmat described little interaction with the crowd, with the show leaning on the songs and visuals rather than between-song conversation.

Rachmat also described orderly entry, from gate checks to the crowd’s passage into the stadium.

Ye closed the night with “Runaway.” Beyond the stage, the concert also had late-night transport support: Medcom reported extended MRT operating hours to help fans get home.

item.title: A$AP Rocky Accused Of Stealing Artist’s Video As AI Controversy Explodes
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: A$AP Rocky faces plagiarism allegations after comparisons between his "Shroom Clouds" video and an older artist's work.
item.content:encoded:
They are calling him “A$AP Copy” now. Not the innovative homie A$AP.

A$AP Rocky may have a bigger problem than angry fans generally complaining about artificial intelligence. An artist is now questioning whether Harlem’s own borrowed somebody else’s creativity without permission. This is a mess…on a Monday.

Rocky’s latest visual, “Shroom Clouds,” featuring reggie and Jeremih, arrived October 19 with the sort of psychedelic imagery we have come to expect from the Harlem fashion icon.  Check. No problem. However, the celebration took a detour into accusations of plagiarism. And this is serious.

Here is the video:

Social media users eventually began circulating comparisons between Rocky’s video and an older piece of visual art reportedly created in 2019 by artist Ari Fararooy. Ari is no chump…he’s a champ. The similarities are beyond startling. Was it reproduced or digitally manipulated? Or simply AI?

A creative director and visual effects artist known online as @cache_bunny (the person that was allegedly infringed on) shared comparisons that attracted considerable attention. The artist subsequently addressed the controversy.

“I’ve gotten over 600 messages about this so far. I don’t know what to do about it yet, but clearly this has struck a major chord with the creator community, which is nice to see. Stealing artists work is not ok, and that’s not the precedent we want to set. I can’t understand why they didn’t just reach out to license the clip, or make their own version inspired by it.

If anyone has advice on what to do please let me know” 

Others jumped on this as well:

WHEW. And then AI enters the chat.

The official production credits acknowledge people specifically identified as AI artists, including Spike and Red, along with Ces. Rocky directed the video alongside Aisulton Seitov and Pietro Biz Biasia. Yeah…this is getting uglier by the moment.

Rocky has acknowledged artists approach AI differently and does not discriminate. He apparently judges each individually. Things change with this.

Rocky has built an enviable reputation for imaginative music videos. Why would someone with so much money and so many creative resources risk that reputation over a visual sequence? It is not even that long.

Perhaps there is an explanation involving licensing, artistic collaboration or something else entirely? Maybe?

Rocky’s camp has not said anything, at the time of this writing.

And until somebody does, the questions will probably multiply faster than the mushrooms in this video.

AI, y’all.

Thoughts?

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Cassie Wins Dismissal From Freak-Off Worker’s $35M Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Cassie exits Clayton Howard's $35 million case as the court grants her dismissal request and gives Diddy a deadline to respond.
item.content:encoded:
Cassie is out of Clayton Howard’s $35 million lawsuit after a judge dismissed the former escort’s claims against her.

Judge Anne Hwang granted the singer’s request on October 21 in Los Angeles, while keeping the case alive against Diddy.

“Defendant Ventura’s motion to dismiss is hereby granted; this will be the order as stated on the record,” the court minutes read.

Howard used the name Dave while working as a male escort and brought his suit against the pair in June 2025.

He alleged Cassie arranged sessions Diddy directed and accused them of using drugs and coercion to exploit him during paid encounters.

Howard’s claims involved sessions in New York, Miami and Los Angeles, with Howard alleging the encounters caused lasting harm.

Bad Boy Entertainment LLC and CeOpco LLC had also sought dismissal, but Judge Hwang granted only part of their request.

Judge Hwang gave Howard 14 days to amend his claims. Cassie’s attorneys had challenged Howard’s amended claims, saying he failed to connect her acts to sex he performed through threats, deception or force.

They pointed to his account of repeated cash payments and return visits, arguing those details undermined his portrayal of Cassie as his trafficker.

The defense also argued Howard’s own complaint described Diddy’s violence and control over Cassie, including his power to decide when the encounters ended.

“These defects are not curable by better drafting or any reframing of the facts,” her lawyers argued in their August brief.

A July ruling had let Howard try again, and he submitted the fifth rewrite of his lawsuit August 3. Howard then asked to swap in another proposed rewrite that removed his claim of 12 hours of confinement in Miami.

Judge Hwang rejected that bid to swap documents, which Howard had made before the court heard the dismissal requests.

The court separately said it would consider Howard’s request to file an additional response to Diddy’s and the companies’ arguments.

Under the October 21 order, Diddy’s deadline to answer falls on November 4, 14 days after Judge Hwang issued the ruling.
